name: Medicine Scholar Study
body:
Associated Skill Heal (Wis)

Basic Study Ability
Heal Conditions (Ex)

You have studied medicine extensively, and can quickly and effectively counteract negative conditions in your patients. Using this ability is a standard action, and expends 1 point of inspiration. You must be adjacent to your patient and must make a Heal check (on which you automatically gain your normal inspiration bonus) to attempt to cure the condition. You cannot use this ability on yourself. If multiple patients are affected by the condition, or multiple conditions are to be cured, each requires a separate standard action and use of inspiration.

The conditions that you can affect are ranked from minor to dire, with each category having an accompanying Heal DC (see below). You cannot take 10 or 20 on the check or receive aid from any creature except another scholar with this ability—or another character with a dedicated healing theme, at the GM’s discretion.

Minor Conditions (DC 15*): fatigued, shaken, and sickened.
Major Conditions (DC 20**): dazed and staggered.
Severe Conditions (DC 25***): exhausted, frightened, and nauseated.
Dire Conditions (DC 30****): blinded, deafened, paralyzed, and stunned.
Notes
If you have at least 5 ranks in Heal, you no longer need to make Heal checks to remove minor conditions (but you must still use a standard action and spend a point of inspiration).
If you have at least 9 ranks in Heal, you no longer need to make a check to remove major conditions.
If you have at least 13 ranks in Heal, you no longer need to make a check to remove severe conditions.
If you have at least 17 ranks in Heal, you no longer need to make a check to remove dire conditions.
Associated Technique
Precision Technique (Ex)

You deal +1 damage against an opponent you have studied with this technique, or +1d6 if that opponent is flat-footed. These damage amounts increase by a like amount at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, to a maximum of +5 or +5d6 at 20th level. This is precision damage and is not multiplied on a critical hit.

Advanced Study Abilities
Anatomical Studies (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Heal Conditions study ability, scholar level 2nd.

Your knowledge of anatomy allows you to deal more damage. Any time you must make a critical hit confirmation roll, you can instead substitute a Heal skill check (using the AC you are trying to hit as the DC). You cannot use this ability against non-living creatures (such as constructs and undead), even if they are not immune to critical hits.

Bone Setting (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Heal 5 ranks, Heal Conditions study ability, scholar level 5th.

Making use of your knowledge of anatomy and healing, you can heal major damage to the body. You may assist in the recovery of permanent Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution damage by resetting the bones of the ability-damaged character. By making a successful Heal check (DC 20 + 3 for each point of ability damage), you convert this permanent ability damage into temporary ability damage. By doing this, you simultaneously convert an equal amount of hit point damage to nonlethal damage. You can attempt a use of this ability no more than once per day for every 5 ranks you possess in the Heal skill, and no more than once per day per individual.

For example: If you wished to convert 3 points of permanent Strength ability damage to temporary Strength ability damage, you would need to make a DC 29 Heal check. The same action would also convert up to 3 points of hit point damage to nonlethal damage.

Healer’s Resistance (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Heal Conditions study ability, scholar level 2nd.

As a healer, your understanding of disease and illness grants you the knowledge to avoid falling to those illnesses and diseases.

You may roll a Heal skill check in place of a saving throw against any disease, mundane or magical, or any effects that cause the nauseated or sickened condition. (This does not negate any damage or other effects from the same attacks that caused these effects.) You cannot take 10 on this skill check. Once you attain 15 ranks in Medicine, you are immune to all mundane diseases, as well as to the nauseated and sickened conditions; however, you must still make saving throws against magical diseases such as lycanthropy and mummy rot.

Poultices (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Heal 3 ranks, Heal Conditions study ability, scholar level 3rd.

You gain the ability to create special healing poultices, comparable to some potions. If you have an alchemist’s kit or a healer’s kit, it takes 10 minutes per poultice to gathering ingredients and prepare each poultice using treated bandages. (This does not expend charges from the kit, as you are assumed to constantly be replenishing the ingredients you need.) Otherwise, it takes one hour per poultice. Each day, you can create and carry a number of such poultices equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). The poultices thus created cannot be applied by anyone but you. After 24 hours, any poultices that have not been used lose their potency. If you spend 1 minute applying one of your poultices to a wounded living creature (thereby expending its use), that creature regains 1d8 hit points for every 3 ranks that you have in the Heal skill. The use of each poultice also requires the expenditure of 1 point of inspiration.

For example: A scholar with 6 ranks in Medicine and an Intelligence of 18 (+4 bonus) can create 4 poultices per day, each of which can cure 2d8 hit points when used.
